source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

chapter_binding.source_omission_reason: Absent from pinned SBLGNT; the parent Fluent already preserves this numbering gap.
chapter_binding.tsw_omission_reason: TSW also lacks these public labels; comparator bytes unchanged.

key_decisions.rationale: Retain the death metaphor and the perfect participle's accomplished coming without identifying the event.
key_decisions.before: Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, some standing here will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God having come with power.”
key_decisions.after: He went on to say, “Truly I tell you, some standing here will not taste death before they see that the kingdom of God has come in power.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he was saying to them, “Truly I say to you, there are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God having come in power.”

key_decisions.rationale: Retain the difficult relationship between Elijah's restoration and the Son of Man's suffering as a question.
key_decisions.before: He said to them, “Elijah does come first and restores all things. Yet how is it written about the Son of Man that he must suffer many things and be treated with contempt?
key_decisions.after: He replied, “Elijah does come first to restore everything. Yet how is it written about the Son of Man that he must suffer greatly and be treated with contempt?
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Elijah indeed comes first and restores all things. And how is it written of the Son of Man that he should suffer many things and be treated with contempt?

key_decisions.rationale: Preserve the unidentified they and scriptural claim without inserting John by name.
key_decisions.before: But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it is written about him.”
key_decisions.after: But I tell you, Elijah has already come, and they did whatever they wanted to him, just as it is written about him.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But I say to you that Elijah has come, and they did to him whatever they wished, just as it is written of him.”

key_decisions.rationale: Follow the plural arrival and seeing in the pinned source; other clarifies the disciples left below.
key_decisions.before: When they came to the other disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and scribes arguing with them.
key_decisions.after: When they reached the other disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and scribes arguing with them.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And coming to the disciples, they saw a great crowd around them and scribes arguing with them.

key_decisions.rationale: Retain the two parties in the question while leaving their exact identification open.
key_decisions.before: He asked them, “What are you arguing with them about?”
key_decisions.after: He asked them, “What are you arguing with them about?”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he asked them, “What are you arguing with them about?”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserve the sequence of violent symptoms, the spirit as agent, and the disciples' inability.
key_decisions.before: Whenever it seizes him, it throws him down. He foams, grinds his teeth, and becomes rigid. I asked your disciples to cast it out, but they could not.”
key_decisions.after: Whenever it seizes him, it throws him down. He foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and becomes rigid. I asked your disciples to drive it out, but they could not.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: and wherever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams and grinds his teeth and becomes rigid. And I asked your disciples to cast it out, but they were not able.”

key_decisions.rationale: Mark Jesus' echo of the father's words as a quotation; keep the unqualified possibility saying.
key_decisions.before: Jesus said to him, “‘If you can’? Everything is possible for the one who trusts.”
key_decisions.after: Jesus said to him, “‘If you can’? Everything is possible for the one who believes.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And Jesus said to him, “‘If you are able’—all things are possible for the one who believes.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserve the coexistence of faith and unbelief and omit tears and Lord absent from this source.
key_decisions.before: Immediately the child’s father cried out, “I trust; help my unbelief!”
key_decisions.after: At once the boy's father cried out, “I believe! Help my unbelief!”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Immediately the father of the child cried out and said, “I believe; help my unbelief!”

key_decisions.rationale: Distinguish the spirit's departure from the boy's resulting condition and retain most rather than all.
key_decisions.before: After crying out and convulsing him violently, the spirit came out. The boy became like a corpse, so that many said, “He is dead.”
key_decisions.after: The spirit cried out, convulsed the boy violently, and came out. The boy lay like a corpse, so that most of the people said, “He is dead.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And crying out and convulsing him terribly, it came out, and he became like a corpse, so that most said, “He has died.”

key_decisions.rationale: Follow the shorter pinned reading with prayer alone; do not import fasting.
key_decisions.before: He told them, “This kind cannot come out by anything except prayer.”
key_decisions.after: He told them, “This kind can come out only through prayer.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “This kind is not able to come out by anything except prayer.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserve the handing-over passive, the human-hands image, repeated killing, and Mark's three-days-later sequence.
key_decisions.before: because he was teaching his disciples: “The Son of Man is being handed over into human hands. They will kill him, and after he is killed, three days later he will rise.”
key_decisions.after: for he was teaching his disciples. He told them, “The Son of Man is being handed over to human hands. They will kill him, and after he is killed, he will rise three days later.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: for he was teaching his disciples, saying to them, “The Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of men, and they will kill him, and when he has been killed, after three days he will rise.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserve the repeated welcome and the widening relation to the sender; not only expresses the contextual contrast.
key_decisions.before: He said, “Whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me. And whoever welcomes me welcomes not only me but the one who sent me.”
key_decisions.after: “Whoever welcomes one child like this in my name welcomes me. And whoever welcomes me welcomes not only me but the one who sent me.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: “Whoever receives one such child in my name receives me, and whoever receives me receives not me but the one who sent me.”

key_decisions.rationale: Retain us as the stated boundary and the attempted/preventive force of the imperfect verb.
key_decisions.before: John said to him, “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him because he was not following us.”
key_decisions.after: John said to him, “Teacher, we saw someone driving out demons in your name. We tried to stop him because he was not following us.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: John said to him, “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him, because he was not following us.”

key_decisions.rationale: Retain the source's repeated us and compact proverbial wording.
key_decisions.before: Whoever is not against us is for us.
key_decisions.after: For whoever is not against us is for us.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For the one who is not against us is for us.

key_decisions.rationale: Express the stated ground of the gift and emphatic assurance without adding in my name from another reading.
key_decisions.before: Truly I tell you, whoever gives you a cup of water to drink because you belong to Christ will certainly not lose their reward.
key_decisions.after: Truly I tell you, anyone who gives you a cup of water because you belong to the Messiah will certainly not lose their reward.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink because you belong to Christ, truly I say to you, he will not lose his reward.”

key_decisions.rationale: Retain little ones, belief, stumbling, and the disturbing comparison; specify millstone size in a note.
key_decisions.before: But whoever causes one of these little ones who trust in me to stumble, it would be better for that person if a large millstone were hung around their neck and they were thrown into the sea.
key_decisions.after: “If anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for that person to have a great millstone hung around their neck and be thrown into the sea.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: “And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe to stumble, it would be better for him if a great millstone were hung around his neck and he were thrown into the sea.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserve the severe bodily image and the repeated destination rather than turn the command into explanation.
key_decisions.before: If your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life maimed than to have two hands and go into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.
key_decisions.after: If your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better to enter life with one hand than to have both hands and go into Gehenna, into the fire that cannot be put out.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life maimed than having two hands to go into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.

key_decisions.rationale: Keep the parallel image while following this verse's shorter source wording without a fire clause.
key_decisions.before: If your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into Gehenna.
key_decisions.after: If your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better to enter life lame than to have both feet and be thrown into Gehenna.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life lame than having two feet to be thrown into Gehenna.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserve the shift from life to kingdom of God and continue the sentence into the quotation.
key_decisions.before: If your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into Gehenna,
key_decisions.after: If your eye causes you to stumble, throw it away. It is better to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into Gehenna,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And if your eye causes you to stumble, cast it out; it is better for you to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye than having two eyes to be thrown into Gehenna,

key_decisions.rationale: Retain the plural possessive and the Isaiah image without changing worm into an abstraction.
key_decisions.before: where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.
key_decisions.after: where their worm does not die and the fire is not put out.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.

key_decisions.rationale: Leave the difficult salt/fire metaphor open and omit the longer sacrificial addition absent from the source.
key_decisions.before: For everyone will be salted with fire.
key_decisions.after: For everyone will be salted with fire.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For everyone will be salted with fire.

key_decisions.rationale: Keep the connected salt images and plural community command without supplying a single interpretation.
key_decisions.before: Salt is good, but if salt loses its saltiness, how will you season it? Have salt in yourselves and be at peace with one another.”
key_decisions.after: Salt is good, but if salt loses its saltiness, how will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and live at peace with one another.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Salt is good; but if the salt becomes unsalty, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
